protocol.name: raum_stage_v1

description.summary: a program that draws its world into one of raum's rooms

protocol.description:
A stage is a client whose toplevel raum does not show as a window while the camera leans back. The client draws its world from raum's camera instead, laid out on a table on the room's floor, and raum sets that picture into the room: a game's battlefield as the room's diorama, in the gallery and in the house view alike. At work, in front, the stage is an ordinary window again and draws from its own camera.
Every vector is in raum's world: its units are the pixels of the front plane at work, y is up, the front plane looks down -z. A camera is ten floats: the eye (3), the direction it looks (3), its up (3) and the vertical field of view in degrees. The client maps its own world onto the table itself: raum does not know how big that world is.
The frame request is what makes a picture usable at all. It goes out right before the commit that carries the frame, on the same connection, so raum knows which camera every buffer it is handed was drawn from, and draws the room around that picture from the same camera.

description.summary: the manager is not needed any more

request.name: get_stage

description.summary: make the toplevel of this surface a stage

request.description: The surface is the main surface of an xdg toplevel. Asking twice for the same surface is a protocol error.

entry.name: already_staged
entry.summary: the surface is a stage already

request.name: frame

description.summary: the camera the next commit was drawn from

request.description: Sent right before the commit that carries a new buffer. `serial` is the serial of the camera event the frame was drawn from, 0 when it was drawn from the client's own camera. `camera` is twenty floats: the camera the frame was drawn from, then the client's own camera (where its own eye is, while it draws from raum's).

event.name: camera
event.description: `view` is fourteen floats: a camera (ten floats), then the table the world lies on: the middle of its top (3) and its width (1). Until the next event every frame is drawn from this camera, with nothing of the world drawn outside the table and nothing where there is no world: the picture's alpha is 0 there, its colour premultiplied. With `serial` 0 the client draws from its own camera again, opaque, and the camera in `view` means nothing; the table still says where its world lies, so the frame request can tell where the client's own eye is.
